articleTitle: Exploring the Factors Influencing of Teachers’ Acceptance of Artificial Intelligence in Higher Education English Teaching
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Education and Intelligent Research (IEIR)
abstract: This research explores the factors influencing English teachers' acceptance of artificial intelligence (AI) in higher education English teaching, extending the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) to include digital literacy and self-efficacy of teachers. Data from 482 Chinese higher education English teachers were analyzed using Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) with SmartPLS. The results indicate that teachers' digital literacy significantly enhances AI acceptance, along with both perceived ease of use and perceived usefulness. These perceptions further boost teachers' self-efficacy in using AI, thereby promoting broader AI acceptance. The findings highlight the critical roles of teachers' digital literacy and self-efficacy in facilitating integration of AI into higher education English teaching.

articleTitle: Exploring the Usage of Token Economy and Peer Review to Select Lab Assistants and Tutors For Computer Science Courses
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Education and Intelligent Research (IEIR)
abstract: Lab assistants and tutors for computer science courses are usually student workers, selected by faculties, to teach a single student or a very small group of students to facilitate their learning. They are essential resources from which students can obtain individualized help. The screening and selection of such student workers has traditionally been done by faculty members without enough consideration of the inputs from students or without a formal process to quantify and qualify student inputs, which we believe, otherwise, can greatly help improve the selection process in terms of efficacy and accuracy. In this paper, we introduce an idea to address this issue by using a student-centered approach incorporating a token economy to select lab assistants and tutors. We think that this idea applies not only to CS courses but also to courses from other disciplines where there is a need for hiring effective student workers to help their peers learn well.

articleTitle: An Enhanced Relation-flow Algorithm for Solving Number Line Problems
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Education and Intelligent Research (IEIR)
abstract: Number line problems (NBLP) constitute an indispensable part of primary mathematics. It remains challenging for existing solving algorithms to solve NBLP due to the lack of specialized algorithms for understanding NBLP text and diagram. This paper presents an enhanced relation-flow algorithm for solving NBLP, utilizing customized syntax-semantics models and a diagram procedure to ensure corresponding problem text and diagram understanding performance. For NBLP text understanding, it uses a syntax-semantics method for extracting relations from the NBLP text by developing a group syntax-semantics model for NBLP text. For NBLP diagram understanding, it proposes a novel diagram procedure for acquiring relations from the NBLP diagram. Thus, a relation group is obtained from the problem text and diagram. Finally, a symbolic reasoner is proposed to infer the relation group and obtain the answer. Experimental results demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed method in solving the number line problem. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first algorithm capable of solving NBLP, making a significant contribution to expanding the scope of solvable problems.

articleTitle: A Game-Theoretic Analysis of AI Integration in Education
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Education and Intelligent Research (IEIR)
abstract: This paper investigates AI integration in the field of education from the perspective of game theory, which focuses on the strategic interactions among three key stakeholders: AI systems, teachers, and educational institutions. Strategies and payoff functions for the three stakeholders are proposed, while considering factors such as enhanced teaching and benefit from AI, and the potential conflicts among the stakeholders arising from AI integration. Our analysis covers both discrete and continuous models to capture the range of strategic interactions and their outcomes. The results reveal the existence of a threshold for the benefit from AI integration to enable cooperation among the stakeholders in AI integration, as well as the collaborative effort required to promote AI integration in education instead of one party making the majority of the effort. Our findings highlight the need for carefully designed AI policies and collaborative strategies to achieve effective AI use in education. This preliminary work hopefully provides a foundation for further research on strategic decision-making and policy development in the field of intelligent education.

articleTitle: Collaborative Learning Environments by Educational Agent Feedback Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Education and Intelligent Research (IEIR)
abstract: The creation of large language models (LLMs) has opened up new possibilities for diagnosing learning progress through artificial intelligence (AI). However, the practical application of LLMs in actual educational diagnostic situations is limited ability to gather learner data in a proactive manner. This research introduces a diagnostic system based on LLMs that improves collaborative learning by simulating tutors. Our system involves two external agents to handle collaborative tasks. The first agent employs a reinforcement learning approach to formulate learning progress assessing and conduct initial diagnoses. The second agent uses LLMs to parse tutoring guidelines by utilizing student online learning record data, to generate simulated dialogues between students and tutors and evaluated the diagnostic abilities of our system. Our system showed impressive performance in both tasks of evaluating learning progress and making differential diagnoses. This research represents a step towards more seamlessly integrating AI into tutor settings, potentially enhancing the accuracy and accessibility of learning diagnostics.

articleTitle: Collaborative Agents for Anxious Depression Diagnosis and Intervention Leverage Neuroimages in Human Brain-AI Interactions
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Education and Intelligent Research (IEIR)
abstract: Depressive disorders to some extent erode the mental and physical health of many individuals. There is a pressing need for new technologies to enhance the diagnosis as well as treatment of depression, which currently relies heavily on subjective reports and lacks precise classification for its subtypes. Anxiety-type depression is a subtype of depression that is clinically challenging to distinguish from non-anxiety-type depression. Statistical data indicates anxiety-type depression has a higher prevalence among university students, poses greater risks, and has more possibility of leading to suicidal tendencies. Research integrating neuroimaging with artificial intelligence for assisted diagnosis and treatment of anxiety-type depression holds significant clinical importance. This study collected fNIRS data from depression patients and evaluated classification performance using a deep learning measure based on the CNN framework, highlighting the extraction of the most significant feature associated with anxiety-type depression deficits. This work provides a valuable lens to understand the complexities of anxiety-type depression and design human-computer interaction treatment methods. Drawing on research in psychology and cognitive science, and recent advancements in cognitive intervention studies, we illustrate the demands of assisted diagnosis, requiring a high degree of intelligent treatment of depression. We propose addressing these demands by designing and integrating a social-assistive chatbot that employs CBT for treating anxiety-type depression into a comprehensive agent system.

articleTitle: A Review on Relation-Flow Approach in Problem Solving
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Education and Intelligent Research (IEIR)
abstract: This review examines the relation-flow approach, an increasingly prominent category of algorithms in problem-solving. The article discusses key assumptions, workflow, and advancements in relation-flow methods, highlighting their advantages over other approaches. It begins by defining essential concepts related to the relation-flow approach and its algorithms. A comprehensive framework for applying these algorithms to problem-solving is then presented. The review traces the historical development of the relation-flow approach, focusing on states and actions (or transforms). Additionally, it explores the approach’s distinct advantages and concludes with insights into future directions for further research and development.

articleTitle: Enhancing Large Language Models for Precise Classification of Teacher Praise Discourse: A Fine-Tuning Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Education and Intelligent Research (IEIR)
abstract: In the field of education, teacher praise, as a form of positive feedback, is regarded as a crucial mechanism for fostering student development and maintaining a positive learning environment. In recent years, large language models, particularly those represented by the GPT series, have achieved breakthroughs across multiple dimensions of natural language processing, demonstrating exceptional capabilities in general language understanding and generation tasks. However, when focusing on fine-grained analysis in specific domains, such as the precise classification of teacher praise discourse, large language models without specialized optimization often fail to achieve optimal performance. To address this, our study proposes a strategy aimed at enhancing the performance of large language models in the teacher praise classification task through fine-tuning techniques. We first established a dataset of teacher praise discourse. Using this dataset, we then conducted targeted training on selected large language models to improve their accuracy and robustness in the teacher praise discourse classification task. Experimental results show the fine-tuned model outperforms baseline models on datasets.

articleTitle: Multi-Knowledge Distillation for Constructing Math Word Problem Encoder
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Education and Intelligent Research (IEIR)
abstract: Technology of solving math word problems is predicted to play an increasingly important role in smart education today. It will be used to help students master complex problem solving faster, promote personalized tutoring, and support the advancement of smart education. The encoder is a very important part of the math word problem solving algorithm. Particularly the BERT encoder based solving algorithms have a good accuracy. However, in educational environments, computational resources are usually limited, and pre-trained models like BERT are difficult to be applied in resource limited scenarios due to the large number of parameters and the huge amount of computation. Therefore, in order to promote the popularization of intelligent education, it is necessary to study small encoder applicable to math problem solving. Knowledge distillation is an effective method of model compression, so this paper applies it to the field of math word problems by combining the knowledge of the layers of the teacher model, as well as the math knowledge of the predictive label through different decoders and the true label to distill a lightweight encoder suitable to be used on small devices. Results of experiment show that with 90% reduction in the number of parameters, the answer accuracy only 11.9% lower than the original BERT in the math word problem solving task and significantly outperforms the existing mainstream small models. This provides strong support for the practical application of algorithms for solving math word problems.

articleTitle: The Effect of Generative Artificial Intelligence on Students’ Academic Achievement: A Meta-analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Education and Intelligent Research (IEIR)
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GAI) technologyhas had a significant impact on teaching and learning, but its actual impact on students’ academic achievement is controversial. This study conducted a meta-analysis to systematically analyze 26 experimental and quasi-experimental articles on the impact of GAI on students’ academic achievement before April 2024. The results showed that: (1) GAI had a moderate positive effect on students’ academic achievement, (2) Compared with other disciplines, GAI can significantly improve the effect of medical disciplines, (3) The effect of GAI on students’ academic achievement was regulated by the sample size, and the medium sample had the higher effect value, (4) Multiple GAI applications over time are more effective than one-time intervention, (5) Compared to assessment feedback and combined application, conversational interactive GAI and content generative GAI are the most widely used and effective, and (6) GAI is applicable to various grade level and users.

articleTitle: The Impact of Teacher Participation in Online English Forums on Middle School Students' Intercultural Communicative Competence
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Education and Intelligent Research (IEIR)
abstract: With the advancement of globalization, the importance of intercultural communicative competence (ICC) in education has become increasingly prominent. This study explored the impact of Online Discussion Forum for Junior Students English (ODF-JSE) on students ’ ICC, based on a study conducted with 39 students and 5 bilingual foreign teachers. A four-month teaching experiment was carried out in a middle school in a Chinese city, adopting Byram's ICC model as the theoretical framework. The study encompassed dimensions of knowledge, skills, attitudes, and critical cultural awareness. Results revealed that ODF-JSE significantly improved students' ICC compared to traditional classroom methods. Both students and teachers positively evaluated ODF-JSE, recognizing its effectiveness in enhancing students' intercultural knowledge, skills, attitudes, and critical cultural awareness. This research contributes valuable insights for enhancing intercultural education practices in secondary English teaching.

articleTitle: Improvement of AI-Driven Deep Knowledge Tracing Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Education and Intelligent Research (IEIR)
abstract: This research aims to assess the application and effectiveness of AI-driven Deep Knowledge Tracing (DKT) technology in vocational education. By integrating LSTM, Bayesian Knowledge Tracing (BKT), and Reinforcement Learning (RL), we developed a hybrid model designed to optimize personalized learning paths. According to the experimental data, this hybrid model considerably improves student learning outcomes compared to the classic BKT and the independent LSTM models. The model demonstrates superior performance in prediction accuracy, knowledge mastery, and error control, highlighting its substantial potential in the vocational education sector. Future research should focus on optimizing this model and its application in a broader range of educational contexts.

articleTitle: Integrating Artificial Intelligence into Whole-Person Education for a New Paradigm in Engineering Education
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Education and Intelligent Research (IEIR)
abstract: This investigation assesses the incorporation of artificial intelligence (AI) within the realm of engineering education, underscoring its congruence with Harvard University's 'Whole-Person Education' framework and the prevailing intelligentization trend in the Digital-Intelligent Era. The study delves into the imperatives, theoretical underpinnings, salient features, and intrinsic challenges of the paradigm shift towards intelligent engineering education. Employing a systematic review methodology, this research synthesizes findings from 82 empirical studies spanning the period from 2011 to 2024, all of which are anchored within the General Systems Theory (GST) framework. The analysis elucidates the complex roles and systemic interplays of AI technologies within the engineering educational paradigm. The paper meticulously articulates the intrinsic nature of intelligent engineering education, accentuating the strategic embedding and profound utilization of intelligent technologies to catalyze the metamorphosis and reconfiguration of engineering educational systems. It categorizes and examines six pivotal AI application domains within engineering education, dissecting their manifestation of pivotal intelligent education characteristics, such as technological synergy, resource amalgamation, and platform convergence. Moreover, the study offers an objective examination of the impediments to the realization of intelligent engineering education, encompassing the enhancement of educational milieus with intelligent features, the reconceptualization of pedagogical and student roles, and the evolution of pedagogical content and approaches. The paper proffered targeted solutions to these challenges, thereby contributing innovative theoretical perspectives and pragmatic directives that are instrumental in propelling academic dialogue and practical strides in educational innovation and quality within engineering education.

articleTitle: Critical Review of AI-Driven Human Research Intelligence: Integrating 3C Theory of Cognition, Emotion, and Thinking in Human-AI Interaction
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Education and Intelligent Research (IEIR)
abstract: This paper offers a short summary and critical review of the forthcoming book "AI-Driven Research Intelligence: Integrating 3C Theory from Foundational Abilities to Advanced Research Thinking". The rapid development of artificial intelligence (AI) technology has transformed scientific research, prompting the need for theories on human-AI collaboration. This book introduces the 3C Theory, which integrates AI with human cognition, emotion, and research thinking (critical thinking, creative thinking, and computational thinking). Within the 3C theoretical model, AI not only as a research tool but as an enhancer of human cognitive abilities, emotional regulation, and research thinking. By comparing 3C Theory with existing models, the book highlights its potential to transform research processes and support the design of intelligent Human-AI research systems. Additionally, this paper explores the prospects of intelligent research system design, proposing new avenues for research innovation through interdisciplinary collaboration and Human-AI interaction.

articleTitle: Evaluating Automated Geometric Problem Solving with Formal Language Generation on Large Multimodal Models
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Education and Intelligent Research (IEIR)
abstract: In recent years, research on automatic analytic geometry problems has gained considerable attention. The key areas of focus include the analysis of natural language problems, graph analysis, and multi-modal information fusion reasoning. With the increasing advantages of large multi-modal models in cross-modal data scenarios, they offer a novel technical approach for solving geometric problems. Unlike traditional rule-based methods, which typically parse problem text and graphics into a formal language and solve them using a symbolic solver, our approach leverages large multi-modal models. In our experiment, we first use these models to integrate text and graphical information, generate the corresponding formal language, and then invite three annotators to evaluate its accuracy. Next, we optimize the formal language using graphical location data and, finally, test the effectiveness of the optimized formal language in solving geometric problems using large multi-modal models with prompt-based inputs. Extensive experiments on public datasets demonstrate that the use of formal languages improves the accuracy of geometric problem-solving in large multi-modal models.

articleTitle: Cross-Disciplinary Cognitive Diagnosis Leveraging Deep Transfer Learning for Smart Education
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Education and Intelligent Research (IEIR)
abstract: Driven by the dual principles of smart education and artificial intelligence technology, the online education model has rapidly emerged as an important component of the education industry. Cognitive diagnostic technology can utilize students’ learning data and feedback information in educational evaluation to accurately assess their ability level at the knowledge level. However, while massive amounts of information provide abundant data resources, they also bring about complexity in feature extraction and scarcity of disciplinary data. In cross-disciplinary fields, traditional cognitive diagnostic methods still face many challenges. Given the differences in knowledge systems, cognitive structures, and data characteristics between different disciplines, this paper conducts in-depth research on neural network cognitive diagnosis and knowledge association neural network cognitive diagnosis, and proposes an innovative cross-disciplinary cognitive diagnosis method. This method combines deep learning techniques and transfer learning strategies to enhance the performance of the model in the target discipline by utilizing the common features of the main discipline. The experimental results show that the cross-disciplinary cognitive diagnosis model based on deep learning performs better than the basic model in cross-disciplinary cognitive diagnosis tasks, and can more accurately evaluate students’ learning situation.

Index Terms: Area Under Receiver Operating Characteristic Curve

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Chinese Large Language Models in Solving Math Word Problems
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Education and Intelligent Research (IEIR)
abstract: Recently, researchers in the field of math word problem (MWP) solving have reported performance metrics for various large language models (LLMs) on benchmark datasets, with some models consistently achieving new state-of-the-art (SOTA) results. However, the benchmark datasets are often selectively curated and subjectively refined, leading to discrepancies between the evaluation metrics and actual experiences in real-world applications. To address this issue, we constructed a comprehensive dataset named AS-Math5k to assess more authentic and reliable performance. AS-Math5k is derived from practical teaching scenarios and encompasses multiple-choice questions and word problems across K-12 grade levels. Subsequently, we developed a unified evaluation framework that includes a prompt engineering module, a problem-solving module, and a result analysis module. This framework evaluates the performance of representative Chinese LLMs on AS-Math5k and provides a detailed discussion of performance variations among LLMs when solving problems of different grade levels and types. Experimental results indicate the following: (1) There is a notable discrepancy in the performance of large language models on real-world MWPs compared to benchmark datasets; (2) LLMs generally perform better on objective problems with clear, standardized answers; and (3) LLMs demonstrate strong comprehension and problem-solving abilities in both explicit relations and logical scenarios.

articleTitle: Application of Artificial Intelligence and UAV Remote Sensing in Regional Vegetation Environment Information Extraction
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Education and Intelligent Research (IEIR)
abstract: The presence of land surface vegetation and buildings plays a crucial role in the urban landscape. The point cloud data collected by LiDAR is an important technical means to rapidly construct regional surface 3D model. However, there are some problems such as high cost and low acquisition efficiency. With AI's rapid progress, new solutions are emerging. In this study, we first collected remote sensing images from unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) to generate dense image matching (DIM) point cloud data. Aiming at the problems such as incomplete noise point removal and poor algorithm universality in the current extraction process of vegetation and buildings, we adopted emerging AI technology to build a multi-feature joint extraction model. The model's effectiveness was demonstrated on an open dataset, showing its ability to separate vegetation from buildings while maintaining 3D extraction efficiency. Finally, we verified the effectiveness of this model with a case study of Guizhou University. This study aims to combine low-cost UAV remote sensing images and artificial intelligence technology to achieve efficient and high-precision extraction of vegetation and building models in a man-machine collaborative way, and provide application potential for realizing regional environmental monitoring related work quickly and effectively.

articleTitle: Emotion-Driven AI Collaboration and Multimodal Learning in Vocational Education
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Education and Intelligent Research (IEIR)
abstract: With the rapid development of artificial intelligence technology, the application of personalized learning systems in vocational education has gained increasing attention. However, existing systems often handle only single-modal data and lack real-time monitoring and adaptive adjustments based on emotional states. To address these issues, this study proposes a personalized learning system based on human-machine collaboration, integrating multimodal data fusion and emotion-driven mechanisms, specifically designed for vocational education. Experimental validation shows that the proposed system significantly improves student learning outcomes and teacher satisfaction, particularly in the areas of complex interdisciplinary knowledge integration and personalized learning path generation. This study provides new insights into the design of personalized learning systems in vocational education and lays the foundation for the application of human-machine collaboration and multimodal data fusion technologies in the educational field.

articleTitle: Dynamic evolution analysis of AI in education based on SciMAT
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Education and Intelligent Research (IEIR)
abstract: The purpose of this article is to conduct an in-depth analysis of literature on AI in education. A bibliometric study was conducted using articles from SciMAT and Web of Science databases, selecting 388 papers published between 1985 and 2023. This study systematically studied and analyzed the literature on the application of AI in education, and found that the number of emerging keywords was significantly higher than the number of annihilated keywords, indicating a growing trend in international research on AI in education. The evolution path of the theme is becoming increasingly complex, involving a wide range of research fields, forming 7 main evolution paths, keywords such as Technology, Chatbot, Experience, and Neural Networks may become research frontiers. By reviewing relevant research on the empowerment of AI in the field of education, we aim to provide reference for further research.

articleTitle: Applying concept of IOT in education environment to increase smart learning quality education: Review paper
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Education and Intelligent Research (IEIR)
abstract: In education, the Internet of Things (IoT) is a hot topic and is becoming increasingly popular across the globe because it is powerful, rapid, interactive, inspiring, individual and comprehensive. Students, educators and administrators have also encountered some critical difficulties with the IoT. Internet of things has begun to bring tremendous challenges and opportunity for the education sector, as it is traditionalist. In addition, IoT problems and issues in education were also addressed in this research. This technology enables students and educators around the world to be linked. This technology encourages teamwork and innovation, enhances access to knowledge, improves safety, and enriches the learning experience of teaching. The study found that IOT helps to shape intelligent lesson plans, smart classrooms, and smart campuses. Technology such as augmented reality, cloud computing for artificial intelligence, and virtual reality has the ability to add tremendous value. Personalization of information has been enabled by ICT technology. Such innovations are more relevant and lead to better planning for the future. Cloud computing center on how learning data can be store and directed toward improvising learning process. IOT and wearable encourage seamless learning. In the current educational market, innovations are becoming increasingly commonplace. Today's education, better teaching, and learning through smart devices was leveraged by new technologies. These innovations move the learning platform to real-time, advanced search, sharing, collaboration, connectivity and enhance the experience of the classroom

articleTitle: Exploration of Computer Aided Education: Development and Application of Digital Course Resources Based on FEM
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Education and Intelligent Research (IEIR)
abstract: This study aims to explore computer aided education and develop and apply digital course resources based on the Finite Element Method (FEM). Vocational engineering design education faces challenges in teaching abstract concepts and motivating student learning. To address this challenge, we used torsion of a hollow cylinder as a case study and utilized FEM to obtain stress and deformation plots with visual characteristics. These digital course resources were integrated into the existing curriculum. Through a combination of anonymous questionnaires and teacher-student discussions, we evaluated the impact of this teaching method on understanding abstract concepts, stimulating discussions, and enhancing interest. Most indicators scored above 4.0/5.0, indicating a high level of effectiveness for this method. Computer-assisted technology has great potential for educational innovation, particularly in the development of digital course resources. Future work will explore the integration of augmented reality, virtual reality, and design-based learning methods to enrich students' learning experiences.

articleTitle: Personalized Art Image Generation Model for Smart Art Education
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Education and Intelligent Research (IEIR)
abstract: With the rise of the wave of smart education, art education is gradually moving towards the transformation stage of personalization and intelligence. Thanks to the rapid development of artificial intelligence technology, the field of education has ushered in unprecedented technological empowerment, opening up new development paths for art education. Personalized art image generation technology can generate customized art images according to students’ learning situation and interest preferences, thus improving the teaching effect and learning experience. However, the existing mainstream technology has problems such as high demand for computing resources, style distortion, and lack of detail expression, so there is still room for improvement in artistic expression. Aiming at the above problems, this paper proposes a personalized art image generation method based on diffusion model. The method uses a stabilized diffusion model as the backbone network, and the model is fine-tuned using LoRA and Dreambooth, aiming to improve the artistic style recognition and detail richness of the generated images. Experimental results show that the method performs well on the task of personalized art image generation, with excellent performance in terms of realism and diversity.

articleTitle: Computational Thinking in Asia-Pacific K-12 STEAM Education: A Systematic Review
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Education and Intelligent Research (IEIR)
abstract: The interest in STEAM (Science, Technology, Engineering, Arts, and Mathematics) education has been growing around the world, which allows the integration of diverse disciplines. Also, computational thinking (CT) is considered as part of the essential skills needed in the 21st century. This review aims to investigate the current state of K-12 STEAM education to develop CT skills, in the context of the Asia-Pacific region and provide examples of best practices. A total of 25 articles met the inclusion criteria for the review, they were published from 2019 to 2023, and employed learning activities developed at preschool, primary and secondary levels. It is also discussed the current benefits and challenges of integrating CT into STEAM education, and it is provided recommendations for practitioners, teachers, and policymakers.

articleTitle: An Intelligent Querying System for Educational Statistics Using Pre-trained and Large Language Models
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Education and Intelligent Research (IEIR)
abstract: Educational statistics play a crucial role in comprehending the current state of educational development and informing decision-making processes. However, traditional data querying systems, which heavily rely on precise SQL statements, often fail to adequately support non-expert users. To address these limitations, we propose an intelligent querying system that leverages a pre-trained language model and a large language model to facilitate natural language interactions for accessing educational statistical data. Our system consists of two main components: query element parsing and SQL statement generation. During the parsing phase, a fine-tuned PLM identifies and correlates relevant tables and elements from the database schema. In the subsequent generation phase, these matched tables and elements, along with the original query, are utilized by LLMs to generate SQL statements. This methodology improves the reliability of SQL generation while mitigating the complexities associated with prompt engineering and reducing the significant costs associated with LLM fine-tuning. The proposed system has been successfully implemented within relevant business units, demonstrating its practicality and effectiveness.

Author Keywords: natural language to structured query language

articleTitle: The Impact of AIGC on Modern Education: Transforming Learning and Teaching Methods
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Education and Intelligent Research (IEIR)
abstract: This paper examines the transformative influence of artificial intelligence generated content (AIGC) on modern education, focusing on its applications for both learners and educators. By leveraging cutting-edge algorithms such as GAN, Diffusion and Transformer, AIGC technologies like ChatGPT and DALL-E enable automated content creation, interactive learning, and multimedia generation. The paper explores the diverse roles AIGC plays in improving educational processes, proposing a methodology of using AIGC to assist learning and teaching. It also discusses the challenges, including the risk of misinformation, academic integrity concerns, the changing dynamics of teacher-student relationships and uncertain results. This study emphasizes the need for ethical integration and critical thinking to maximize the positive effects of AIGC in education.

articleTitle: Data Augmentation with Large Language Models For Math Word Problem Solving
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Education and Intelligent Research (IEIR)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a method to enhance the problem-solving capabilities of models for Math Word Problems (MWP) using data augmentation with large language models. We aim to implement this method effectively; thus, three specific techniques are introduced: Data Augmentation Method Based on Probability Threshold, Iterative Correction-Based Problem Equation Generation, and Augmented Data Screening Based on Scoring Rules. These methods are applied at different stages before, during, and after the data augmentation process to achieve the best results. Overall, our approach works as follows: the model’s problem-solving ability is tested on the validation set by a certain step during the training, in order to collect both the problem types which the model struggles with and the instances which the model fails to solve. This data is then augmented using a large language model. After appropriate processing, this augmented data is integrated into the training set for subsequent training. Experimental results show that our method demonstrates superior performance on various datasets, with accuracy exceeding that of the baseline.

articleTitle: A Study of Automatic Solver for Math Word Problems based on RoBERTa and SW-MSA
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Education and Intelligent Research (IEIR)
abstract: In this paper, we encountered the major challenge of effectively solving Mathematical Word Problems (MWP) that involve complex logic and long text descriptions. To address these issues, we proposed the following methods: 1.Introduced a RoBERTa encoder optimized with a dynamic masking technique to enhance the understanding of MWP text. 2.Developed a decoder based on Shifted Window Multi-head Self-Attention (SW-MSA), which limits the self-attention computation range while effectively capturing long-range dependencies, thereby improving decoding efficiency and accuracy. By combining these methods, we proposed a new RoBERTa-SWMSA model. Experimental results show that the RoBERTa-SWMSA model performs excellently on standard datasets Math23k and Ape210K, with notable advantages in solving problems with complex logic and long text descriptions. Ablation experiments further highlight the importance of the pre-training strategy for model performance. The RoBERTa-SWMSA model provides an efficient, accurate, and generalizable solution for the automatic solving of MWP.

articleTitle: RoBERTa-based Multimodal Sentiment Analysis of Detecting Teachers’ Emotions
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Education and Intelligent Research (IEIR)
abstract: Multimodal sentiment analysis, which combines data from various sources such as text, images, and audio, has become a vital tool in educational settings for monitoring teachers’ emotions in the classroom and ensuring teaching quality. We propose a novel model called RoMSA (RoBERTa-based Multimodal Sentiment Analysis) to enhance the effectiveness of this process. RoMSA utilizes a new multimodal joint embedding mechanism that fully captures cross-modal information, and it incorporates a Random Modal Masked Language Modeling (RMMLM) task to improve the model’s understanding of different modalities. By leveraging the extensive textual knowledge obtained during pretraining, RoMSA significantly improves the accuracy of multimodal sentiment analysis. Tested on the CMU-MOSI and CMU-MOSEI datasets, RoMSA achieved state-of-the-art results, demonstrating its effectiveness in detecting and analyzing emotions. Through the analysis of teachers’ emotions during classes, multimodal sentiment analysis models can output teachers’ emotional states, helping to ensure teaching quality and enabling educators to optimize their teaching methods to maintain a positive classroom atmosphere.

articleTitle: Integrating Educational Assessment and Generative AI for Personalized Knowledge Building: An Exploratory Study
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Education and Intelligent Research (IEIR)
abstract: This study investigates the integration of educational assessment (EA) and generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) for personalized knowledge building in online learning environments. We propose a framework that combines cognitive diagnostic assessment with constrained GenAI to create tailored learning experiences. Our web-based system, built on content from an international assessment study, evaluates learners’ skill mastery and generates personalized remedial content. The preliminary results demonstrate the system’s capacity to provide detailed skill mastery information and generate adaptive remedial questions. While long-term efficacy research is ongoing, initial findings suggest that this EA-GenAI integration enhances the personalization and effectiveness of online learning. This study advances adaptive learning technologies by exploring innovative applications of AI for personalized assessment and dynamic content creation.

articleTitle: Research on the Evolution of Public Sentiment and the Implementation Strategy of the "Double Reduction" Policy
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Education and Intelligent Research (IEIR)
abstract: The " double reduction" policy is the first major decision made by the national common prosperity strategy in the field of education in the new era. An in-depth understanding of the evolution of public sentiment and main concerns after the introduction of the "double reduction" policy is the guarantee for the implementation of the policy and one of the bases for "educating the public to be satisfied". Based on the text data of social networks three months after the introduction of the "double reduction" policy, this paper carried out sentiment analysis and cluster analysis to identify and characterize the public's feelings and attitudes towards the "double reduction" policy. On the whole, the public sentiment is more positive than negative, and it has gone through three stages: the initial confusion period, the dividend enjoyment period, and the exploration contradiction period. In this regard, it is proposed that the implementation of the "double reduction" policy in the future needs four key changes: from "management" to "service" - refining the policies of the education management department, doing a good job in family education guidance, from "pressure" to "incentive" - promoting the reform of school classroom teaching, building a teacher incentive mechanism, from "blocking" to "guiding" - setting up capital traffic lights in the education and training industry; Broaden the way out of talents, from "phenomenon" to "cause" - deepen the reform of educational evaluation and reduce parents' anxiety about performance.

articleTitle: Framework Design of a Multi-Educational-Agent System for University Lecturers
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Education and Intelligent Research (IEIR)
abstract: Lecturers play a crucial role in students' learning activities. Their teaching planning, understanding of students' situations, and teaching methods all impact student success. The use of artificial intelligence in education is growing, but there is limited research on AI solutions to assist lecturers' daily work. Current research lacks a comprehensive intelligent system to assist lecturers in dynamically tracking student learning, supporting them in research and teaching, and assisting them in applying for resources from the university. This paper proposes a framework design for a virtual teaching and research intelligence system for university lecturers. The system offers personalized guidance to students, real-time feedback on student learning to lecturers, assists with teaching planning, optimizes working time, and aids in scientific research. Meanwhile, the proposed system design can also optimize the allocation of campus educational resources to alleviate conflicts caused by traditional manual allocated methods.

articleTitle: The Importance of Modular Structure in Artificial Intelligence Algorithm Evaluation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Education and Intelligent Research (IEIR)
abstract: With the fast development of Artificial Intelligence (AI) algorithm, the AI algorithm evaluation approach, which only uses model performance as the evaluation criterion, is not appropriate anymore. Firstly, the performance-based evaluation strategy is difficult to deeply explore the fundamental contribution of the internal structure of AI algorithms to the problem solving; secondly, a complete process needs to be designed for each evaluation, which leads to a large amount of time and energy invested by researchers. In order to evaluate AI algorithms in a more efficient and standardized way, this paper combs through the current patterns of AI algorithm evaluation and deconstructs them into highly modular components to meet different experimental needs.

articleTitle: Trends in Geographic Information Science Discipline in The Era of Artificial Intelligence and Big Data
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Education and Intelligent Research (IEIR)
abstract: Geographic Information Science (GIS) serves as a technical tool for studying geography, remote sensing, and surveying and mapping science. Besides, GIS supports key applications such as environmental monitoring, resource management, and urban planning. As such, the continued development of GIS research is critical to advancing both the related research field and its practical applications. However, the complexity of geographic information presents significant challenges to existing modeling methods. Recently, the surge of data and the rapid progress of artificial intelligence (AI) technology have brought new ideas and opportunities for the development of GIS. Therefore, this paper systematically reviews the current research and emerging trends in the application of AI and big data within GIS, identifies key research issues and challenges ahead. The findings demonstrate that AI and big data have shown a positive and steady impact on GIS research. This work seeks to promote the integration of new technologies and methods in GIS, facilitating its further research and practice.

articleTitle: A review of Machine learning-based Trojan detection techniques for securing IoT edge devices
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Education and Intelligent Research (IEIR)
abstract: With the rapid advancements on the Internet of Things (IoT) and its applications, the need for securing IoT devices against network intrusions has become increasingly important. Among the primary threats to these devices are denial of Service (DoS) attacks. One effective method for detection of intrusions and DoS attacks is the application of machine learning. Machine learning enables cybersecurity systems to analyze patterns, allowing organizations to allocate their resources more effectively and secure their networks. This study reviews machine learning-based techniques for detecting Trojans to enhance the security of IoT edge devices. Our study focuses on reviewing machine learning-based Trojan detection methods for IoT device security. Our approach involves conducting a literature review of relevant articles and collecting data from these articles. The gathered data is analyzed for classification and verification purposes.

articleTitle: Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Cybersecurity and Inhibitors to AI Adoption
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Education and Intelligent Research (IEIR)
abstract: This review examines Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Cybersecurity. The purpose of this examination is to identify and contrast AI advancements in Cybersecurity, areas for improvements, and inhibitors to advancing the use of AI for Cybersecurity. AI has seen exponential growth and advancement in innovation and automation in recent years and security professionals are benefiting from implementing and using AI based Cybersecurity tools. There are implementation concerns for data privacy, security vulnerabilities and AI biases resulting from training data AI is dependent on for learning. There are also trust issues between humans and machines. This study aims to provide a structured evaluation of AI advancements in Cybersecurity and AI adoption concerns. It does this by reviewing current and relevant academic articles from January 2022 to January 2024 on AI in Cybersecurity and recommend ideas for further studies. The comparison and contrast revealed advancements in AI Dataset are needed, such as Realtime datasets and Privacy Datasets, to teach AI about privacy. Improvements in Explainable AI (XAI) is needed to provide algorithm transparency and provide insights into AI decision-making process and outcomes. A key adoption issue is Data Privacy, closely followed by performance and accuracy of AI algorithms. Trust is another key issue at the centre of most studies. The review also identifies future research opportunities in emerging cybersecurity application areas, AI components and awareness of AI inhibitors for the successful adoption of AI-based cybersecurity.

articleTitle: AI in Education for Corporate Training
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Education and Intelligent Research (IEIR)
abstract: The gap between employer demands and the skills highlighted on resumes reveals a major flaw in traditional university education. The current one-size-fits-all approach leaves graduates unprepared for the fast-evolving job market. To address this, we are developing an AI-powered personalized learning platform tailored to corporate training. This platform utilizes a machine learning model that analyzes individual resumes to generate customized course maps based on the user’s unique background and career goals. By aligning educational pathways with specific job requirements, it caters to the growing need for job-specific programs, especially among Gen Z. A Logistic Regression Model is trained on resume datasets to predict suitable professions for users, while tools like Gensim and TensorFlow help construct personalized knowledge graphs of relevant courses. Various graph-based algorithms like PageRank, SimRank, and HITS are used to generate an optimized study map, considering course difficulty and prerequisites. This innovative approach offers a significant leap in helping job seekers refine their skills and meet employer expectations. The platform's findings could ultimately be integrated into corporate training programs, enhancing workforce development and addressing the shortcomings of traditional education systems.

articleTitle: How LLMs Support EFL Writing:A Case Study of K-12 English Learning Based on the EDIPT Model
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Education and Intelligent Research (IEIR)
abstract: Large Language Model (LLMs), the most stylish pre-trained language-agency model, has recently garnered unprecedented global attention. However, the rapid growth of LLMs’ exceptional performance in understanding and comprehending human language and completing various tasks conversationally has sparked debates regarding its educational implications and applications. Notably, it serves as a language consultant, companion, and assessment expert in Chinese English education, utilizing suggestions to enhance the quality of listening, speaking, reading, and writing instruction. This study is one of the initial efforts to explore the potential contribution of LLMs to the instruction and acquisition of writing English as a Foreign Language (EFL) in K-12. As a result, the study proposes a response strategy framework that combines the EDIPT model to promote and support future English learning development in K-12 education. Additionally, applying an LLMs can improve learning efficiency, reduce the teacher’s burden, and support large-scale personalized learning, the other side also brings challenges such as weakened learning motivation, less reliability of knowledge, and privacy and security issues. To enhance the writing abilities of EFL students for K-12, it is recommended that educators work alongside LLMs to provide feedback on students' writing in a generating.

articleTitle: A Learning Style-aware Dropout Prediction Method via Fusing Global and Local Semantics
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Education and Intelligent Research (IEIR)
abstract: Massive Open Online Courses (MOOCs), with their vast resources and significant flexibility, have emerged as the most popular way for online education globally. However, one of the emergent challenges faced by numerous MOOC platforms is the high rate of dropout. While many approaches have been proposed to predict dropout rates, the common drawback is that they usually ignore the theories from educational psychology when modeling the behavior from log data, deriving undesirable performance for the task of dropout prediction. In this paper, we propose a novel learning style-aware framework for predicting dropout on MOOCs, effectively fusing global and local semantics contained in learners’ learning behaviors. First, the learning styles are identified by clustering on time series data in logs of MOOCs. Then, the global and local semantics contained in the learning style information and learning behavior information are captured by a module of CNNs, deriving the meaningful hidden representations. Finally, the obtained high-quality representations are used to derive the predicted dropout behavior given learner-course pairs. Extensive experiments are carried out on the KDD Cup 2015 dataset, and the results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A Review of AI-based Techniques in Online Course Recommendation: Metrics, Factors, and Research Methods
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Education and Intelligent Research (IEIR)
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive literature review of online course recommendation systems, focusing on studies published between 2019 and 2023 across various academic databases. We selected and analyzed relevant research, covering key areas such as AI methods, research questions, influencing factors, and evaluation techniques. AI methods for course recommendation are categorized as traditional and advanced approaches. Traditional methods include Content-Based (CB) recommendation, Collaborative Filtering (CF), and related techniques, while advanced methods encompass deep learning and reinforcement learning (RL) techniques. Advanced AI methods demonstrate the ability to manage more complex data structures and provide more accurate and personalized recommendations compared to traditional methods. The common research challenges identified include accuracy, cold start, data sparsity, information overload, dynamic interest recommendation, and interpretability. We further analyzed the factors considered in these systems by categorizing user and course attributes. User attributes are divided into five categories: Demographic Information, User Behavior, Personal Preferences, Knowledge and Skills, and Emotional State and Social Interaction. Course attributes are categorized into four types: Course Metadata, Course Evaluation, Knowledge and Skills, and Social Influence. The most commonly used evaluation metrics include Recall (R), Precision (P) and F1-Score (F), which are straightforward to interpret and facilitate comparison across different studies. Additionally, we highlight future research directions, providing insights for further academic exploration in this domain.

articleTitle: Designing a LLM-driven Avatar System to Enhance Social Skills for Autistic Children in DTT Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Education and Intelligent Research (IEIR)
abstract: Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) is a psychological condition with unknown causes, challenging treatment, and an increasing prevalence rate. A typical characteristic of this disorder is impaired social interaction or communication. In current autism treatments, there are significant challenges and obstacles, such as a shortage of professionals, long treatment cycles, and substantial financial costs. To address these issues, we design a avatar system for individual training sessions for autistic children. We aim to reduce economic burdens while helping autistic children develop core social skills—specifically, self-introduction—while also alleviating the workload of autism therapists and improving treatment efficiency. In this paper, we employ the Discrete Trial Teaching (DTT) method, which is the most commonly used technique in Applied Behavior Analysis (ABA). We enable our avatar figures with the rapidly advancing large language models (LLMs) and speech services in artificial intelligence, to create a comprehensive and high-performance individual training session for teaching self-introduction to children with autism. Our evaluation results show that this system is fully functional with excellent performance. We also plan to explore future improvements including a comprehensive facial expression dataset for children with autism and applying the system into clinic practices.

articleTitle: Optimising Incidental Vocabulary Learning through Task Type, Language Proficiency, and Semantic Elaboration in Intelligent Education
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Education and Intelligent Research (IEIR)
abstract: This study examines the intricate relationships between task type, semantic elaboration, and learner proficiency on the incidental acquisition of vocabulary in English for Specific Purposes (ESP) within the context of computer-assisted learning environments. A cohort of 127 Business English learners engaged in a range of tailored tasks aimed at fostering comprehensible output and enhancing language production skills. Subsequent assessments measured their ability to recognise and recall vocabulary items. While individual task processing factors did not attain statistical significance in isolation, a salient interaction emerged between task types and learner proficiency levels, highlighting the pivotal role of proficiency in moderating the impact of task type on vocabulary acquisition. By focusing on vocabulary acquisition through language production, this research addresses a significant gap in current literature, which tends to prioritise comprehension over production in CALL. The findings underscore the imperative of integrating task type and learner proficiency considerations into the design of intelligent language learning interventions, offering nuanced understanding of the complex dynamics between focus-on-form, semantic elaboration, and proficiency in ESP settings.

articleTitle: Predicting Dropout on MOOCs via Characterizing Personalized Learning Ability and Course Difficulty
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Education and Intelligent Research (IEIR)
abstract: Due to their extensive resources and high flexibility, Massive Open Online Courses (MOOCs) have emerged as a popular way of online learning for millions of people across the world. However, the high dropout rate has been identified as one of the critical issues related to many current MOOCs platforms. While numerous approaches have been suggested for predicting dropouts, most of existing methods simply focus on analyzing learners’ behavioral information, which ignore the impact of learner-specific learning ability and course difficulty, leading to the undesirable predictive performance. In this paper, we propose a novel deep learning-based model for dropout prediction, in which a multi-task learning structure is created to optimize the utilization of students’ learning strengths and course challenges for hidden representation learning. More specifically, predicting students’ learning ability and predicting course difficulty are modeled as two subsidiary subtasks within the framework of multi-task learning. Consequently, the supportive information is fully used for learning high-quality representations for the task of dropout prediction. Comprehensive experiments are conducted on the real-world dataset KDD CUP 2015, these findings highlight the efficacy of the suggested approach.

articleTitle: A Pilot Study On Detecting Cognitive Load Using Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks With EEG Signals
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Education and Intelligent Research (IEIR)
abstract: Cognitive load detection is a critical part of cognitive state research, aiding in the understanding of the brain's response to stimuli in the cognitive process. Electroencephalogram (EEG) is a valuable tool for viewing brain states under varying cognitive loads. This study proposes a cognitive load detection approach based on Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KANs), a novel neural network architecture, utilizing multi-channel EEG signals. The five different types of features (raw EEG signals, temporal statistical features, time-frequency features, entropy features, and deep features) are used as inputs to explore the efficiency of three KAN-based detection models (KAN, fast-KAN, & Cheby-KAN). Furthermore, this study investigates the effect of different channels on the detection performance using different feature inputs. The experiments are conducted using a 19-channel EEG dataset from a mental arithmetic task. The results demonstrate the proposed KAN-based models outperform existing state-of-the-art deep learning-based methods (e.g., EEGNet & CNN-BiLSTM), achieving an accuracy of 98.26% and an F1-score of 98.30%. KANs obtain better performance than MLPs as classifiers at the decision-making layer in this EEG classification task. Moreover, the later channel selection experiments reveal that the selected subsets of channels hold the potential to achieve similar performance to the full set of channels.

articleTitle: Integrating Question Proficiency Level and Historical Knowledge States for Knowledge Tracing
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Education and Intelligent Research (IEIR)
abstract: Knowledge tracing focuses on modeling the progression of students’ knowledge states based on their past response records and predicting their next performance. However, most RNN-based knowledge tracing models struggle to capture long-distance dependencies within sequences, leading to a decline in performance. Besides, most models ignore the personalized question proficiency level of students when solving problems. To tackle these challenges, we propose a new knowledge tracing model that incorporates question proficiency levels and historical knowledge states (QHKT). Firstly, the TCN is employed to respectively extract the students’ answering speed and result features at multiple time steps, which are then fused to obtain the personalized question proficiency level of the students. Subsequently, based on the proficiency level, we utilize LSTM network to acquire the refined knowledge states of the students. To alleviate the long-distance dependency problem, a carefully designed sparse attention mechanism is used to aggregate multiple historical knowledge states to obtain a more precise representation of knowledge states, and predictions are made based on this. We extensively validate the proposed method on two public datasets, and the results demonstrate that QHKT outperforms existing models, achieving better knowledge tracing effect.

articleTitle: A Review of Taxonomy Expansion And its Applications in AI empowering research
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Education and Intelligent Research (IEIR)
abstract: Taxonomy Expansion refers to adding new concepts or categories on the basis of the existing classification framework to better reflect the hierarchical structure of the knowledge system.Taxonomy Expansion, as a very important downstream task of Natural Language Processing (NLP), has a very wide range of applications in the field of AI empower research. In this paper, we analyze the key techniques of taxonomy expansion based on deep learning frameworks and the applications of taxonomy expansion in AI empower research in recent years in chronological order and increasing order of technical complexity. We systematically analyze the advantages and disadvantages of each technique, as well as the selection of datasets, and finally make an outlook on the future research and application direction of each technique. In recent years, generalized reviews of taxonomy expansion techniques are rare, and this review can help researchers better understanding the key techniques in taxonomy expansion and their applications in AI empowering research, and promote the in-depth application of AI in research.

articleTitle: Unified Knowledge Tracing Framework for Subjective and Objective Assessments
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Education and Intelligent Research (IEIR)
abstract: With the continuous deepening and development of the concept of smart education, learners’ comprehensive development and individual needs have received increasing attention. However, traditional educational evaluation systems tend to assess learners’ cognitive abilities solely through general test scores, failing to comprehensively consider their actual knowledge states. Knowledge tracing technology can establish knowledge state models based on learners’ historical answer data, thereby enabling personalized assessment of learners. Nevertheless, current classical knowledge tracing models are primarily suited for objective test questions, while subjective test questions still confront challenges such as complex data representation, imperfect modeling, and the intricate and dynamic nature of knowledge states. Drawing on the application of knowledge tracing technology in education, this study aims to fully utilize examination data and proposes a unified knowledge tracing model that integrates both objective and subjective test questions. Recognizing the differences in question structure, assessment methods, and data characteristics between objective and subjective test questions, the model employs the same backbone network for training both types of questions. Simultaneously, it achieves knowledge tracing for subjective test questions by universally modifying the training approach of the baseline model, adding branch networks, and optimizing the method of question encoding. This study conducted multiple experiments on real datasets, and the results consistently demonstrate that the model effectively addresses knowledge tracing issues in both objective and subjective test question scenarios.

articleTitle: Enhanced Graph-Based Model with Mathematical Knowledge Embedding for Math Word Problem Solving
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Education and Intelligent Research (IEIR)
abstract: Math Word Problems (MWPs) represent a critical area of research in natural language processing and artificial intelligence, with the goal of translating natural language descriptions into mathematical expressions and deriving solutions. Despite recent progress with graph-based and tree-based neural models, many approaches still struggle to capture the implicit mathematical knowledge embedded in these problems. This limitation impedes their ability to accurately represent the problem-solving process, especially for complex MWPs that require an understanding of implicit mathematical relationships. To tackle this challenge, we propose integrating mathematical knowledge directly into graph neural network models to enhance their effectiveness in solving intricate MWPs. Specifically, we introduce a formula graph where each formula is abstracted into a graph structure and integrated into an enhanced model, thereby facilitating efficient resolution of MWPs involving implicit knowledge. Our approach aims to improve model performance on complex MWPs, as demonstrated through empirical evaluation on the Ape210K dataset.

articleTitle: AI-Empowered Human Research Integrating Brain Science and Social Sciences Insights
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Education and Intelligent Research (IEIR)
abstract: This paper explores the transformative role of artificial intelligence (AI) in enhancing scientific research, particularly in the fields of brain science and social sciences. We analyze the fundamental aspects of human research and argue that it is high time for researchers to transition to human-AI joint research. Building upon this foundation, we propose two innovative research paradigms of human-AI joint research: "AI-Brain Science Research Paradigm" and "AI-Social Sciences Research Paradigm". In these paradigms, we introduce three human-AI collaboration models: AI as a research tool (ART), AI as a research assistant (ARA), and AI as a research participant (ARP). Furthermore, we outline the methods for conducting human-AI joint research. This paper seeks to redefine the collaborative interactions between human researchers and AI system, setting the stage for future research directions and sparking innovation in this interdisciplinary field.

articleTitle: Artificial Intelligence for Research (AI4R): Knowledge Base and Impact
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Education and Intelligent Research (IEIR)
abstract: Artificial Intelligence for Research (AI4R) has recently emerged as the fifth research paradigm, exerting a significant impact across various fields. This paper aims to provide an overview of the current applications of AI4R, laying the groundwork for a knowledge framework that elucidates its components and characteristics. We will explore emerging research models enabled by AI4R, discuss tools developed through AI4R-based MAN-AI collaborations, and assess how these innovations have enhanced existing research capabilities. Finally, the paper identifies key trends driven by AI4R.

articleTitle: Research on Multimodal Knowledge Points Segmentation Tool for Classroom Teaching Videos
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Education and Intelligent Research (IEIR)
abstract: Knowledge points represent the fundamental units of teaching information or concepts and serve as the foundation for teaching content. The segmentation of knowledge points from extensive classroom teaching videos by integrating artificial intelligence technology can assist educators comprehend the way in which course content is presented and teaching methods are employed. However, due to the complexity of teaching scenario and the fact that knowledge points presentations contain multimodal information, there have been few studies conducted to analyze the correlation between the knowledge points and the multimodal features and to segment the video clips from the perspective of the knowledge points. In light of the above, this paper proposes a novel multimodal knowledge points segmentation tool for classroom teaching videos. The tool has three main functions, which are designed to achieve intelligent segmentation and extraction of knowledge points. These include extraction of candidate knowledge points sequence fusing auditory and textual features, extraction of candidate knowledge points sequence based on visual features and segmentation of knowledge points integrating multimodal information. It provides teachers with a convenient platform and method for segmenting knowledge points, thus enabling them to conduct a series of teaching analyses.
